title: Late-binding volume locks + CNI stall — incident diary and runbook draft
content:
Summary:

A production cluster experienced a slow-moving scheduling backlog on 2024-11-14 that manifested as a spike in Pending pods and a correlated increase in node memory pressure. Root cause (short): interaction between our late-binding CSI driver (rbd-flexor variant) holding volume attach locks longer than expected when CNI (flannel overlay) packets were dropped, which prevented kubelet from completing Pod teardown/attach sequences and left ephemeral mount/staging state that bled kernel memory and filehandles. Result: node kernel memory and oom_score_adj churn, kube-proxy memory jitter, and a scheduler backlog as nodes reported NotReady/OutOfDisk-ish signals.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture on-call timeline and temporary mitigations applied
- Draft a short runbook for future responders (stopgap + long-term)
- List follow-ups and engineering tickets

High level timeline (UTC):
- 2024-11-14 01:03 — Pager: sustained p95 pod scheduling latency > 5s, spike in Pending pods; first pager threshold crossed.
- 01:06 — Oncall investigating: observed dozens of pods in Pending on two clusters (us-west-2-primary, us-east-1-canary).
- 01:12 — Noticed many kubelet logs reporting "stage/unstage volume timed out" and repeated CSI attach/detach loops.
- 01:25 — CNI flannel logs show repeated CNI Add/Del hang and retransmits for pod CIDRs on the affected nodes.
- 01:34 — Node memory pressure metrics show kernel memory growth /fd count growth on 8 nodes; two nodes return NotReady briefly.
- 01:42 — Mitigation applied: cordon + drain of the two worst nodes to clear scheduling backlog for other nodes.
- 02:10 — Restarted flannel daemonset on affected nodes (rolling restart) — improved CNI packet path, but volume attach stuck state persisted for a while.
- 03:00 — Manual cleanup: forced CSI detach via controller side tool for 6 PVCs; forced kubelet restart on 4 nodes.
- 04:20 — Cluster stabilized; scheduler backlog cleared, pod evictions and restarts normalizing.

Key signals and logs we used:
- kubectl get pods --all-namespaces | grep Pending — list of stuck pods
- journalctl -u kubelet | grep -E "stage|unstage|volume|attach|detach" — repeated timeouts (~120s)
- flanneld logs from daemonset pods showing CNI Add delay and systemd-resubmit errors
- node-exporter: kernel_memory_failcnt and processes_fds_count spike (prometh-based alerts)
- kube-scheduler metrics: scheduler_queue_length and schedule_attempts_total p95
- Container runtime events: repeated Mount failures followed by Attach success after long delay

Root cause analysis (hypothesis and supporting evidence):
1) Primary chain: transient CNI packet loss/hanging during a network fabric maintenance window caused flannel to drop or delay CNI Add/Del operations. Evidence: correlating cloud provider network maintenance logs with increased packet drop metrics; flanneld retransmit logs at the same time window.
2) While CNI Add/Del stalled, CSI driver attempted late-binding attach/teardown operations that rely on kubelet/container runtime callbacks. With CNI not completing pod network setup, kubelet had multiple in-flight mount/unmount flows that remained in an indeterminate state. Evidence: kubelet logs show VolumeStaging operations blocked waiting on NodePublish call which never completed; controller-manager shows volume attach stuck in "attached" state for longer than normal.
3) The indeterminate state caused file descriptor and kernel memory growth on affected nodes (open mounts/loops). This trended into kernel OOM pressure for some pods and slow garbage collection in kubelet. Evidence: node-exporter fd_count up 3x; kernel memory pagesize counters rising; dmesg shows "Memory cgroup out of memory" on two nodes.

Why scheduler backlog formed:
- A subset of nodes reported NotReady/NetworkUnavailable or had artificially high allocatable pressure due to kubelet marking ephemeral resources degraded. Scheduler reattempts and requeues pods, causing queue growth.
- Evictions created churn that further saturated the controller reconcile loops.

Immediate mitigations we used (runbook-style steps executed during incident):
1) Assess scope: query Pending pods by node affinity and list PVCs attached to Pending pods.
   - kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase==Pending -o wide --all-namespaces
   - kubectl get pv,pvc -A | grep <pod-labels>
2) If a node shows kernel-memory growth and stuck volume ops: cordon and drain gracefully (evict pods to healthy nodes), unless time-sensitive low-latency workloads require manual action.
   - kubectl cordon <node>
   - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force (use caution)
3) Restart CNI on affected nodes (rolling): delete flannel pod on node and let daemonset recreate. Monitor flannel logs for successful CNI ADDs.
   - kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l app=flannel --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
4) If CSI controller shows attach stuck, use controller-side detach helpers or controller logs to force detach stale attachments. Make small batches (3-6) to avoid thrashing.
5) If kernel memory or fd counts remain high, restart kubelet and/or CRI on node after cordon; prefer kubelet restart first to preserve mounts state where possible.
   - sudo systemctl restart kubelet
   - sudo systemctl restart containerd
6) Reintroduce node after stabilization: uncordon once mounts are clean and CNI healthy.
   - kubectl uncordon <node>

Temporary mitigations we recommend adding to runbook (short-term):
- Add a triage checklist item: "If Pending pods + stage/unstage timeouts + CNI errors, suspect late-binding volume + CNI interaction".
- Add an automated paged alert rule that combines: Pending pods > X and node fd_count > Y across nodes to reduce noisy single-signal alerts and accelerate correct ownership.
- A small utility script for oncall that gathers: kubelet journal snippet (last 300 lines), flannel logs for node, CSI controller attach list, node fd_count and memory stats. (See quick-scrape below.)

Quick-scrape script (ops helper) — output commands only (oncall copy/paste):
- kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase==Pending -o wide
- for node in $(kubectl get nodes -o name | cut -d/ -f2); do echo "--- $node ---"; kubectl exec -n kube-system ds/flannel -c flannel -- sh -c "echo logs for $node"; done
- kubectl logs -n kube-system deployment/csi-controller -c controller --since=2h | egrep "attach|detach|error"
- ssh node && sudo lsof -p $(pgrep kubelet) | wc -l && sudo cat /proc/meminfo | egrep "Anon|PageTables|KernelPageTable"

Longer term fixes and engineering tickets (proposed):
- FIX-1823: Make CSI driver resilient to delayed CNI; ensure Attach/Detach state machine tolerates long-running network setup.
- NET-953: Investigate flannel edge cases with transient packet loss -> add backoff/retry metrics and avoid blocking node-level operations.
- SRE-1248: Add a node-level watchdog that alerts before fd_count / kernel memory crosses dangerous thresholds; allow automated cordon if configured.
- DEVS-3010: Add a graceful kubelet mount/cleanup subcommand for late-binding drivers to forcibly clear stale mounts after N minutes.

Open action items (owners assigned):
- Arjun Rao: Create FIX-1823 ticket with reproducer notes and initial test plan (due 2024-11-25).
- Sofia Kim: Add aggregated alert for Pending+fd_count and draft Slack runbook snippet (due 2024-11-20).
- Liam O'Connor: Add additional telemetry around controller attach durations and expose percentile metrics (due 2024-12-05).
- Maya Patel (me): Produce a compact ops helper script and stash in repo at github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-ops/tools/volume-cni-scrape (WIP).

Post-incident recommendations for oncall playbook (short):
- When you see the characteristic triple: Pending spike + kubelet stage/unstage timeouts + CNI ADD/DEL errors — escalate to SRE Pager and include the CNI and CSI leads.
- Prefer cordon+drain for worst nodes early; avoid mass kubelet restarts without cordon (causes scheduling storms).
- Use controller-side detach helpers only in small batches.
- After stabilization, create a timeline and capture sample logs in the incident channel for future RCA.

Notes / unresolved questions:
- Why did the CSI controller not force-detach faster? Is that a safety threshold we can tune?
- What specific flannel condition leads to CNI Add blocking higher-level operations? Need kernel/netstack deeper trace.
- Reproducer attempt blocked in staging environment due to lack of identical network fabric — we should consider a chaos test for late-binding+network-loss sequence.

Appendix: quick kube commands used during triage (for copy/paste):
- kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase==Pending -o wide
- kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/flannel -l app=flannel --all-containers --tail=200
- kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/csi-controller --since=3h | head -n 200
- kubectl describe node <node> | egrep "Non-terminated Pods|Allocatable|Capacity|Conditions"
- ssh <node> sudo systemctl restart kubelet  # only after cordon and agreement

End of diary — keep this as the working runbook draft until FIX-1823 and NET-953 have PRs attached.

Scratchpad: quick hypothesis checklist for future responders:
- Are Pending pods co-located with PVCs? -> yes/no
- Are there CNI Add/Del errors within the same timeframe? -> yes/no
- Is attach duration > 2m? -> yes/no
- Node fd_count > baseline by 2x? -> yes/no
- Did restarting CNI fix packet path? -> yes/no
